headline: TWO DAYS RUNNING, AND STILL ONLY ONE SET OF KNUCKLES TO BLAME
subhead: Sheriff Cole Ironside on a second near-silent day in Gasket, spoiled by the very same troublemaker.
body:
Well, dear reader, I near had it again. A whole Monday stretched out ahead of me quiet as a held breath, same as yesterday, and for a good long while I let myself believe this town had finally learned to behave. I even had my boots up on the porch rail. Then, same as clockwork, came the one holler I've come to dread: YK, throwing another punch into the stillness like the hush itself was an insult. One brawl. That's all it takes to ruin a man's whole afternoon of peace.

I'll grant you, one scrap in a day is about as close to a miracle as this rusted-out town gets. But it does gnaw at me that it's the same troublemaker two mornings straight now, like YK's made a career of being the last domino standing between Gasket and a full day of nothing. Mark my words, I keep careful track of who won't let a good quiet lie, and that name's earned itself a spot at the top of my ledger.

We did get a new face creaking in through the dust today too — IRON-CFAD, fresh off whatever road brought it here, standing at the edge of town like it's still deciding whether Gasket's worth the trouble. Ain't thrown a fist yet that I've heard of, so I'll extend the same courtesy I'd give any newcomer: a wary nod, and a warning that the hush around here don't last. Lord knows my own joints creak something awful most mornings — a man my age gets stiff standing sentry so long, is all, nothing more to read into it.

So I'll take my near-quiet Monday and be grateful for the mercy it was, same as I was grateful yesterday, and the day before that this town had honest folk in it who knew how to let a place rest. One clanker's temper shouldn't spoil two good mornings running. And yet here we are.
